context.objective: Enable employees to submit expenses in the existing employee portal for policy-based approval and Finance payment handling.
context.current_task: Review the evidence-backed ExpPay requirements and resolve material workflow and policy unknowns.
in_scope: Employee expense submission in the existing employee portal
Approval routing based on payment method and amount
Finance handling of corporate-card payment and out-of-pocket payroll reimbursement
actors: Employee — submits expenses and may revise/resubmit rejected expenses
Direct manager — approves expenses when required by the supplied rules
Next-level manager — approves expenses of $101 or more
Finance — handles reimbursement and uses QuickBooks expense types for tax reporting
systems: QuickBooks (expense types are the category authority; interface is unknown)
Payroll (out-of-pocket reimbursement destination; interface is unknown)
Corporate-card payment process (vendor-neutral; interface is unknown)
authoritative_sources: E-001: stakeholder opening statement supplied in this exercise
E-002: stakeholder follow-up answers supplied in this exercise
confirmed_business_rules: Employees submit expenses in the existing employee portal; managers approve them; Finance handles reimbursement.
Corporate-card expenses of $25 or less are automatically approved.
Corporate-card expenses from $26 through $100 require the employee's direct manager.
Corporate-card expenses of $101 or more require the direct manager and next-level manager.
Non-corporate-card expenses always require the direct manager and also require the next-level manager at $101 or more.
Expense categories mirror QuickBooks expense types used by Finance for tax reporting; no additional category-specific limits are defined.
Receipts are required for expenses of $26 or more.
Corporate-card expenses are paid directly to the card vendor, and requirements remain vendor-neutral.
Approved out-of-pocket reimbursements use the employee's next scheduled payroll deposit.
Rejected expenses can be revised and resubmitted.
Expenses must be submitted within 60 days.
derived_facts: Payment method and amount must be available to apply approval and receipt rules.
A non-corporate-card expense under $101 has only the stated direct-manager approval requirement.
A receipt is not required at $25 or less because the stated required threshold starts at $26.
constraints: Use the existing employee portal for employee submission.
Mirror QuickBooks expense types for Finance tax reporting.
terminology: Corporate-card expense — an expense paid using a corporate card.
Out-of-pocket expense — an expense not paid using a corporate card and reimbursed through payroll.
Direct manager — the submitting employee’s direct manager.
Next-level manager — the manager above the employee’s direct manager.

open_questions.question: Which date starts the 60-day submission period, and is the 60th day inclusive?
Which currency governs the dollar thresholds, and how are conversion and rounding handled for other currencies?
Must direct-manager approval precede next-level-manager approval, and what happens after either manager rejects?
How are direct and next-level managers resolved, including vacancies, unavailable managers, and delegation?
What authoritative QuickBooks expense-type list and update process must ExpPay mirror?
What payroll cutoff/calendar behavior applies when approval occurs near or after a scheduled deposit?
On resubmission, which prior approvals remain valid, if any?
Which receipt formats and validation criteria are acceptable?
What employee/manager/Finance status visibility, notifications, audit retention, and reporting are required?
What interfaces connect the portal, hierarchy, category source, card-payment process, and payroll?

decision_debt.decision: Define the 60-day measurement date and inclusive boundary.
Define currency, conversion, and rounding semantics for thresholds.
Define ordering and rejection behavior for two-manager approval.
Define manager resolution, delegation, and unavailable-manager behavior.
Approve the authoritative QuickBooks expense-type list and update process.
Define payroll cutoff/calendar interpretation of the next scheduled deposit.
Define whether approvals reset when a rejected expense is revised and resubmitted.

decisions.decision: Use ExpPay as the project name.
